title: {{NAME}} and the Most Unusual Cup in History
moral: Fairness matters more than victory, especially when nobody is watching.

pages.content:
The Annual Cross-Realm Cup had been running for fifty years: a football tournament played on the meadow between the human town and the Thornwood, with teams from both.

This year: a dispute about the rules.

The fairy team had filed a complaint that the human team's boots gave unfair traction advantage. The human team had filed a complaint that the fairy team's ability to fly gave unfair aerial advantage.

Neither complaint was wrong.

The referee, who was a very old Stegosaurus who had been neutral arbitrator for thirty years, called for a rules committee.

{{NAME}} was appointed chair.

pages.content:
The rules committee met three times.

{{NAME}} discovered that the humans were right about aerial advantage (fairies had scored 40% of their goals through headers impossible for ground-bound players), and the fairies were right about boot traction (the pitch data showed humans covered significantly more ground in the same time).

"The solution," he said at the third meeting, "is not to limit either side. It's to redesign the pitch to equalise the advantages."

Everyone looked at him.

"The humans play on grass. The fairies play on a raised platform that restricts their flight height. Each plays at their strength but within limits."

pages.content:
The modified pitch was built in four days, with the Stegosaurus providing structural support for the raised platform, which it turned out was exactly what a creature of that size was excellent at.

The match was extraordinary: humans sprinting across the lower pitch, fairies darting around their elevated zone, with shared space in the middle where both could meet.

{{NAME}} played centre midfield, which meant moving between levels.

He scored one goal on the lower pitch and assisted a fairy goal on the upper.

Half time: two all.

pages.content:
The game ended three all, which the Stegosaurus declared the correct result for a fairness demonstration match.

Both teams looked uncertain about this.

"You wanted fair," said {{NAME}}. "Fair means this time, the result matches the effort, not the advantage."

Both teams thought about it.

The fairy captain landed on {{NAME}}'s shoulder. "The cross-realm rules stay?"

"Every year," said {{NAME}}. "Ask the referee."

The Stegosaurus nodded once, which settled the matter.

pages.content:
Walking home, {{NAME}} thought about fairness and how hard it was to build from scratch when everyone had different advantages.

Not impossible. Just specific.

In bed, he drew the split-level pitch design in his notebook.

He fell asleep before he finished it.

In the morning, the notebook was open to the half-finished page, and somewhere in the Thornwood, the fairies were practising the aerial game on their designated platform.

Even the morning after, fairness needed maintaining.
